title: Transform Columns and Rows

header.html: Select appropriate column data types; Create and transform columns; Group and aggregate rows; Pivot, unpivot, and transpose data; Convert semi-structured data to a table
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

toc.title: Convert semi-structured data to a table

html:
1Select appropriate column data types

A column's data type controls what you can do with it. Set the type in the Power Query Editor with the data type icon in the column header or with Data Type on the Transform tab.

Why the type matters Effect
Aggregation Numbers can be summed and averaged; text cannot
Sorting Text sorts alphabetically, so "10" comes before "2"
Relationships The two key columns need the same type
Compression Numbers and dates compress better than text
Type Use it for
Whole Number Counts and integer keys
Decimal Number General measurements
Fixed decimal number Money, with four digits after the decimal point
Date, Time, Date/Time Calendar values; remove the time part from a date key
Text Names and codes
True/False Flags

Power Query adds a Changed Type step when it detects types. Check it, because a column left as Any has no type. If dates or numbers come in another culture's format, such as day before month, use Data Type, then Using Locale and pick the culture. Converting without the right locale can produce errors or swapped days and months.

Exam tip

. Relationship key columns must have the same data type, and a date key should have no time part. Use Using Locale when the source format follows another culture.

2Create and transform columns

New columns come from the Add Column tab. Most transformations are on the Transform tab.

Feature Use it when
Custom Column You can write an M expression
Column From Examples You type sample results and Power Query infers the rule
Conditional Column You need if, else if, else rules without writing code
Index Column You need a row number, starting at 0, 1 or a custom value
Split Column One column holds several parts: split by delimiter, by number of characters or by positions
Merge Columns You join columns with a separator into one new column
Extract You need the length, first or last characters, a range, or text before, after or between delimiters

Merge Columns replaces the selected columns with the new one. M is case-sensitive: if, then and else must be lowercase and column names must match exactly.

let
    Source = Sales,
    Margin = Table.AddColumn(Source, "Margin", each [Amount] - [Cost], type number),
    Size = Table.AddColumn(Margin, "Size", each if [Amount] >= 1000 then "Large" else "Small", type text)
in
    Size
Exam tip

. Conditional Column is the no-code choice for if-then rules, Column From Examples infers a rule from samples, and Custom Column needs an M formula. Pick the one the requirement words allow.

3Group and aggregate rows

Group By collapses many rows into one row per group. It is on the Home tab and the Transform tab. In the basic dialog you choose one column to group by and one aggregation. The advanced dialog allows several group columns and several aggregations.

Operation Result
Sum, Average, Median The total, mean or middle value of a column
Min, Max The smallest or largest value
Count Rows The number of rows in each group
Count Distinct Rows The number of different values in a column
All Rows A nested table of the group's rows, which you can expand

Group By also reduces granularity: grouping order lines by store and day gives a smaller table, which helps model size (module 8). Remember that grouping loses the detail of the original rows, so keep the detail if reports need it.

Exam tip

. Group By makes one row per group; All Rows keeps the detail as a nested table. Use Count Rows for row counts and Count Distinct Rows for different values.

4Pivot, unpivot and transpose

These commands change the shape of the table. They are on the Transform tab.

Command What it does
Pivot Column Turns the values of one column into new column headers; you choose a values column and an aggregate function such as Sum, Count or Don't Aggregate
Unpivot Columns Turns the selected columns into Attribute and Value rows
Unpivot Other Columns You select the columns to keep; every other column is unpivoted, including columns added to the source later
Unpivot Only Selected Columns Unpivots only the named columns; columns added later are not unpivoted
Transpose Rotates the table: rows become columns and columns become rows

A report needs tall, tidy data with one row per fact, such as Product, Month and Amount. A sheet with one column per month is wide, so unpivot it. Pivot is the opposite and is used to make a summary layout.

Transpose does not keep the headers as headers. Run Use Headers as First Row first if you need the old headers as data, then Transpose, then Use First Row as Headers. Transpose also resets the data types, so set them again.

Exam tip

. When new columns will keep arriving, use Unpivot Other Columns and select only the columns to keep. Pivot Column needs an aggregate function, and Transpose needs Use First Row as Headers afterward.

5Convert semi-structured data to a table

JSON and XML hold nested data. Connect with the JSON or XML connector, or, for a column that holds JSON or XML text, use Parse on the Transform tab and choose JSON or XML. Power Query shows three nested kinds:

Kind What it is What you do
Record One row of field and value pairs Expand it into columns
List An ordered series of values To Table first, or Expand to New Rows
Table Rows and columns Expand the columns you need

The usual path is: connect, drill into the data, convert a List with To Table, expand the records into columns, expand the lists to new rows, then set the data types. Expand to New Rows repeats the parent row for every item in the list.

let
    Source = Json.Document(File.Contents("C:\Data\Orders.json")),
    AsTable = Table.FromList(Source, Splitter.SplitByNothing(), {"Order"}),
    Expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(AsTable, "Order", {"Id", "Total"})
in
    Expanded
Exam tip

. A list becomes a table with To Table, a record is expanded into columns, and a list column is expanded to new rows. Parse turns JSON or XML text in a column into records.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A source file stores dates as day, month, year, and Power BI Desktop in the US culture turns some of them into errors. What should the analyst use?

  • AUse Change Type with a day-first locale
  • BUse Replace Errors and retype the dates
  • CUse Conditional Column to swap the parts
  • DUse Fill Down to copy the correct dates
Show the answer

Answer: A. Change Type with Locale reads the dates in the format of the culture you choose.

S2An analyst needs a Size column that shows Large when Amount is at least 1,000 and Small otherwise, and cannot write code. Which feature should be used?

  • AIndex Column on the Amount column
  • BMerge Columns on the Amount column
  • CSplit Column on the Amount column
  • DConditional Column on the Amount column
Show the answer

Answer: D. Conditional Column builds if-then-else rules in a dialog without any code.

S3A table has one row per order line. The analyst needs one row per store with the total Amount and the number of rows. Which transformation fits?

  • APivot Column, with Store as headers
  • BGroup By on Store with Sum and Count
  • CUnpivot Columns, keeping the Store
  • DRemove Duplicates on the Store column
Show the answer

Answer: B. Group By on Store with Sum of Amount and Count Rows returns one row per store.

S4A worksheet has one column per week of sales, and a new week column is added every Monday. The model needs one Week column and one Amount column. Which choice keeps the query working at each refresh?

  • AUnpivot Only Selected Columns on the weeks
  • BTranspose, then Use First Row as Headers
  • CPivot Column with Product as the headers
  • DUnpivot Other Columns, keeping Product
Show the answer

Answer: D. Unpivot Other Columns unpivots every column except Product, so new week columns are included.

S5A table lists Region, Category and Amount in rows. The analyst needs one column per Category with the sum of Amount for each Region. Which command should be used?

  • APivot Column on Category, summing Amount
  • BUnpivot Columns on Category and Amount
  • CGroup By on Category and Region, All Rows
  • DTranspose, then use the first row as headers
Show the answer

Answer: A. Pivot Column turns the Category values into column headers and applies the Sum aggregate.

S6A JSON file loads in the Power Query Editor as a list of records. What should the analyst do next to get rows and columns?

  • APivot the list on its first record
  • BTranspose the list into a single row
  • CConvert it to a table, then expand it
  • DGroup the list by its number of records
Show the answer

Answer: C. To Table turns the list into rows, and expanding the record column creates the columns.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which command turns the values of one column into new column headers?

Show the answer

Pivot Column.

R2Which unpivot command also unpivots columns added to the source later?

Show the answer

Unpivot Other Columns.

R3Which Group By operation returns a nested table of the group's rows?

Show the answer

All Rows.

R4What must you do after Transpose to get headers back?

Show the answer

Use First Row as Headers, and set the data types again.

R5Which option reads dates in another culture's format?

Show the answer

Change Type, Using Locale.

R6What do you use to turn a list column into new rows?

Show the answer

Expand to New Rows.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Data types affect aggregation, sorting, relationships and compression; Fixed decimal number for money; Using Locale for other cultures
New columns Custom Column (M), Column From Examples, Conditional Column (no code), Index Column
Split and merge Split by delimiter, characters or positions; Merge Columns with a separator; Extract
Group By Sum, Average, Median, Min, Max, Count Rows, Count Distinct Rows, All Rows (nested table)
Pivot values become headers; needs an aggregate function
Unpivot Unpivot Other Columns includes later columns; Only Selected Columns does not
Transpose rows and columns swap; then Use First Row as Headers and reset types
Semi-structured Parse for JSON or XML; To Table for a list; expand records and lists
